message.content: The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. In most mammalian cells, you can expect roughly **1,000 to 5,000 mitochondria per cell**. Cells with high metabolic activity—such as muscle fibers, neurons, or liver hepatocytes—can contain even more, sometimes exceeding **10,000 mitochondria each**. Conversely, cells with lower energy requirements may have fewer mitochondria.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "Identify the number of the mitochondria in a cell." They likely want the typical number of mitochondria per cell. We should provide an answer. No tool needed. Just give the number. Probably around 1000-5000 per cell depending on type. Provide range and context.
